properties.name: Chablis
properties.summary: Steely, mineral Chardonnay from ancient Kimmeridgian limestone — the northernmost outpost of Burgundy, geographically isolated ~80km northwest of the Côte d'Or.
properties.style: Lean, crisp, flinty. Oyster shell, green apple, citrus. Unoaked or old oak.

properties.name: Côte de Nuits
properties.summary: A narrow limestone escarpment south of Dijon, home to Burgundy's greatest red Grands Crus — Chambertin, Musigny, Romanée-Conti.
properties.style: Rich, structured, dark-fruited reds with extraordinary aging potential.

properties.name: Côte de Beaune
properties.summary: Produces Burgundy's greatest white wines alongside elegant reds. Montrachet, Meursault, Corton are the benchmarks.
properties.style: Whites: rich, nutty, mineral. Reds: softer and more supple than Côte de Nuits.

properties.name: Côte Chalonnaise
properties.summary: Outstanding value — Mercurey, Givry, Rully, and Montagny offer Burgundian quality at fair prices.
properties.style: Lighter, earlier-drinking than the Côte d'Or but with real terroir character.

properties.name: Mâconnais
properties.summary: A large, warm southern zone producing accessible Chardonnay, including the famous Pouilly-Fuissé.
properties.style: Ripe, approachable whites with stone-fruit and floral notes. Usually unoaked.
